sections.heading: 1. Farmer's carry + ball squeeze
lines: ① Hold a shopping bag in each hand.
② Stand tall and walk slowly for 30 sec.
③ Squeeze a soft ball, 5 sec × 10 reps.
④ 2–3 times a week, nothing heroic.

slides.heading: Worth an assessment if

caption:
Koko versus the jam jar, round three. Research suggests grip strength is linked with overall strength and how well people manage everyday life as they age. It isn't the whole story, but it's a handy marker.

It's also one of the easiest things to train. Try a 30-second walk carrying shopping bags, or squeeze a soft ball while the telly's on. Two or three short sessions a week is plenty.

If one hand is weaker, tingly or dropping things more often, get that checked before more squeezing at home. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can fit grip into a broader strength plan. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
